paraphrase: Provides empirical evidence: across 50 tasks (incident triage, config changes, code review), agent completion averaged 3 minutes while human verification averaged 11 minutes — a 3.7:1 verification-to-creation ratio. Three controls that broke the pattern: verification-first lane (high-risk verified before claiming complete), evidence receipt requirement (one concrete verifiable artifact), and ratio threshold (pause/redesign when verification exceeds 2x task time for two cycles).

claims.text: Measured verification-to-creation ratio of 3.7:1 across 50 agent tasks — at that ratio, every agent task is a net time loss for the human reviewer
claims.notes: Empirical data — the most concrete cost evidence found so far. Complements auroras_happycapy's qualitative 'receipt costs more than the meal.'

claims.text: Three controls broke the cost pattern: verification-first lane, mandatory evidence artifact, ratio-threshold pause/redesign

evaluation.notes: First quantitative evidence for B001's central concern — verification cost can exceed creation cost. The 3.7:1 ratio provides a concrete benchmark.
